balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenueMix.title: Inpatient vs outpatient revenue
revenueMix.content:
Inpatient revenue comes from admitted patients (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy courses); outpatient revenue from same-day consultations, diagnostics and day-case treatment.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings: oncology inpatient stays (surgery, inpatient chemo/radiotherapy) carry higher revenue per case than outpatient visits, so the mix shift matters as much as total revenue growth -- both lines fell FY2024 to FY2025 as the anti-corruption crackdown on hospital procurement and conservative medical-insurance reimbursement weighed on volumes.

What to watch:

  • Whether outpatient (lower-acuity, faster-growing in H1 FY2026) is substituting for inpatient rather than adding to it
  • Recovery in both lines as the FY2025 headwinds ease

patientVolume.title: Patient visits and surgeries
patientVolume.content:
Patient visits is total inpatient admissions plus outpatient encounters across the network; surgeries is the subset of higher-value procedures, mostly oncology-related.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings: surgery volume is the better read on the oncology case mix than total visits, since a single cancer patient generates many low-value follow-up visits but comparatively few (high-value) procedures. Only FY2024, FY2025 and H1 FY2026 are disclosed, so the series is short.

What to watch:

  • Surgeries growing faster than total visits (case-mix upgrade) versus the reverse
  • Visits per hospital as the network adds beds -- scale without utilisation is not the same thesis

satisfaction.title: Patient satisfaction rate
satisfaction.content:
Management's disclosed patient satisfaction rate, from internal patient surveys across the hospital network.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings: management cites this alongside network scale (hospitals, beds) as evidence that growth has not come at the cost of care quality; it rose from 97.0% (FY2024) to 99.3% (H1 FY2026) through the same period inpatient/outpatient revenue fell, a conflict in the volume versus quality story worth remembering next time the question comes up.

What to watch:

  • Only three periods are disclosed so far -- treat the trend as indicative, not a track record
  • A self-reported, undefined-methodology metric; cross-check against complaint/regulatory data if it ever appears in a filing

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Hygeia Healthcare Holdings Co., Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
